title: Air-fryer lamb chops
subtitle: Rosemary and garlic-rubbed lamb chops cooked fast in the air fryer.
excerpt: Lamb loin or rib chops rubbed with rosemary, garlic, and olive oil, then air-fried at high heat for browned, slightly charred edges and a pink centre. Ten minutes from seasoning to plate. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Lamb chops are a traditional British and Mediterranean cut, well-suited to high, dry heat. Rosemary and garlic is the classic pairing. The air fryer produces the char of a hot grill without the need to manage a barbecue or griddle.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the rubbed chops in the fridge for up to 4 hours for deeper flavour.

content.text: Lamb chops are best eaten pink. The air fryer's high, dry heat gives you a browned crust fast without needing a hot griddle. The fat cap on a rib chop will render and crisp in 10 minutes at 200°C. Bring chops to room temperature before cooking so the bone doesn't act as a cold sink.

items.prepNote: cut into individual chops, about 4 chops per serving from a French-trimmed rack

content.text: Rub the lamb chops with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt, cracked black pepper, and a small handful of finely chopped fresh rosemary. Leave for 10 minutes at room temperature. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Cook the chops for 5 minutes, flip, and cook for a further 4-5 minutes for medium-rare. Rest for 3 minutes before serving with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Temperature too low or chops not placed fat-side against the basket.
items.fix: Make sure the fat cap is facing the heat source. Air fryers vary in where they direct hot air; try standing the chops upright on the fat edge for the first 2 minutes.
This is actually the correct result for medium-rare. If you prefer medium, add 2 minutes.
Lamb chops are best at medium-rare to medium. Well-done lamb is noticeably drier and tougher.

content.text: Lamb chops in the air fryer are one of the fastest proper dinners possible. Ten minutes including resting. Good with roasted new potatoes cooked in a second round, or with a simple salad. The same method and timing works for pork chops.
